post.title: Autospawn Clone
post.hook: A sales-agent product rebuilt locally, with Claude as its real backend brain.
post.summary: A local clone of the Autospawn outbound-sales platform, built to study its UX. It started as mock data and gained a real Next.js backend where the Claude Agent SDK sources leads, with a deterministic fallback.
post.writeup:
## What it is
A local clone of autospawn.com, an AI outbound-sales platform that finds customers the moment they want to buy. It was built to study the product's UX. All data is fictional.

## Why
To learn how the product's flows fit together: the dispatch composer, campaigns, lead dossiers, watcher, inbox, analytics, sequences, profile and ICP, and credits and plans. The README lists 10 cloned features, plus the landing page and login screen.

## How it works
It is a Next.js 16 App Router app with Tailwind v4 and TypeScript. Design tokens live in `app/globals.css`, with a shared UI kit and two shells, one for the workspace and one for settings.

The backend started as client-side state and now runs through route handlers under `app/api/`. State lives in a single-user JSON store with atomic writes and a credit ledger. It started on better-sqlite3, but the native module segfaulted under some sandboxed launchers, so the store is pure JS.

Lead sourcing and sequence writing run through the Claude Agent SDK, which uses the local Claude Code login when no API key is set. Every agent call has a deterministic fallback generator, so the app works with no auth. Responses carry `via: "claude" | "fallback"`.

Credits are enforced server-side: dispatch costs 24, more-leads costs 8, and an empty balance returns HTTP 402. Composio can optionally power a live Connections catalog.

## What is still simulated
- Signal ingestion has no pollers
- Sequences are drafted, never sent
- Watcher alerts never fire on a schedule
- Contact enrichment comes from the agent, not data vendors

## Open questions
The README flags that "Autospawn" is another company's brand, so it needs a rebrand before any public deploy. It also notes that claude.ai subscription login can't ship to end users, so API-key auth would be needed.
